_comment: MJSL walkway scoring settings. This is the ONLY file you need to edit to change numbers. Change numbers only: keep the quotes, commas and brackets. Lines starting with _comment are notes and are ignored. If something is wrong the app tells you what, in plain words, when it starts.

indicators._comment: Each indicator becomes a barrier from 0 (no problem) to 1 (total obstacle). 'noProblemAt' is the value that gives barrier 0, 'totalObstacleAt' the value that gives barrier 1; in between it is a straight line. 'dimension' says which group the indicator belongs to: physical, sensory, cognitive, economic, socio_cultural (social) or political (participation).

width._comment: Usable width in metres (OSM tags width or sidewalk:width). 1.80 m or more is fine, 0.90 m or less is a total obstacle.

noise._comment: Noise in dB, measured or estimated. 55 dB or less is fine, 85 dB or more is a total obstacle.

slope._comment: Slope in percent (OSM tag incline), sign ignored. 4 % or less is fine, 12 % or more is a total obstacle.

rest._comment: Distance in metres from the segment to the nearest bench. Within 50 m is fine, 200 m or more is a total obstacle.

surface._comment: Barrier per surface type (OSM tag surface), from 0 to 1. A surface not in this list counts as 'no data', never as 0.

economic._comment: The barrier is the share (0 to 1) of the segment that runs next to terraces (outdoor_seating=yes) or parking. 'bufferM' = how close, in metres, counts as 'next to'.

transit._comment: PHYSICAL (person with reduced mobility): public transport within autoData.places.transitRadiusM metres, counted by MODE (bus, tram, metro). Two or more modes is fine (as the client asked), one mode is half an obstacle, none is a total obstacle.

crossings._comment: SENSORY (visually impaired or neurodivergent person): quality of the nearest pedestrian crossing within autoData.places.crossingRadiusM metres. Equipped (traffic lights or tactile paving) = 0, plain marked crossing = 'marked', unmarked = 'unmarked'. No crossing nearby is 'no data' (a street without crossings is not a bad crossing).

glare._comment: SENSORY (glare): barrier per floor material, from 0 (matt) to 1 (very reflective). STARTING GUESSES, to be replaced by measurements. A surface not listed is 'no data'.

signage._comment: SENSORY (signage): guideposts, information boards and maps within autoData.places.signageRadiusM metres. 2 or more is fine, none is a total obstacle.

freeServices._comment: ECONOMIC (low-income person, free services): distance in metres to the nearest FREE service (drinking water, free toilets, library, community or youth centre, see autoData.places.freeServiceAmenities). 150 m or less is fine, 800 m or more is a total obstacle.

legibility._comment: COGNITIVE (allophone person, legibility of the route): sinuosity = length of the segment divided by the straight distance between its ends. 1.10 or less is a clear line, 1.60 or more is a winding, hard-to-follow one.

infoCentres._comment: COGNITIVE (allophone person, information centres): distance in metres to the nearest tourist or information office (open-data tourist offices and OSM tourism=information offices). 300 m or less is fine, 1500 m or more is a total obstacle.

poverty._comment: SOCIAL (co-presence, social class of households): poverty rate of the neighbourhood (IRIS, % of households under the poverty line, 2014 open data). It describes the AREA, not the street itself: a street in a poor area is not worse built, it is where public investment and mixing are most at stake. 15 % or less is fine, 45 % or more is a total obstacle.

participation._comment: POLITICAL (representation, co-participation, projects): is there a formal co-participation device where the segment lies, i.e. inside a priority neighbourhood (QPV, with its citizens' council) or the perimeter of an urban project (ZAC, projet urbain partenarial, NPRU, with legal consultation). Inside = 'inside'; outside = 'outside', which means 'no device identified', not 'no participation'.

thresholds._comment: SOCIAL (memoire dimension 5, 'seuils filtrants': two, three, five steps without a ramp at the entrance of a place are a silent filter). Counts the flights of steps with no ramp that lie within autoData.places.stepsNearPlaceM metres of the segment AND next to a shop, cafe or other place. 0 is fine, 2 or more is a total obstacle.

surveillance._comment: SOCIAL (memoire dimension 5, hyper-visibility and control devices: cameras pointed at the access, gates): number of cameras and gates within autoData.places.cameraRadiusM metres. None is fine, 3 or more is a total obstacle. OpenStreetMap lists only part of the cameras, so a low value does not prove there are none.

coPresence._comment: SOCIAL (memoire dimension 5, co-presence: a pavement wide enough to walk side by side). Width in metres taken ONLY from an OSM width tag or a measurement, never from the estimated default. 1.50 m or more is fine, 1.00 m or less is a total obstacle.

shelter._comment: SOCIAL (memoire dimension 5, small habitable thresholds: porches, awnings, sheltered benches where you can stop without being in the flow): number of sheltered places (bus shelters, shelters, covered ways, arcades) within autoData.places.shelterRadiusM metres. 1 or more is fine, none is a total obstacle.

publicPrivate._comment: ECONOMIC (memoire dimension 4: rest, shade and views that are free versus conditional on buying something): around the segment (autoData.places.publicPrivateRadiusM metres), the share of the PRIVATE places (terraces, cafes, restaurants, bars) among all places that are either free and public (benches, drinking water, free toilets, shelters, parks, gardens, playgrounds) or private. 0 = only free public places, 1 = only private ones. Without any such place nearby it stays 'no data'.

lighting._comment: SENSORY (light is one of the memoire ambiances: luminous gradients, dark or over-exposed zones): can you see where you are going after dark. The barrier is the share (0 to 1) of the segment with no street lighting. Taken from the OSM tag lit (yes = 0, no = 1); without it, from the street lamps mapped within autoData.places.lampRadiusM metres (then labelled 'estimated'). Without any lighting data it stays 'no data'.

landmarks._comment: COGNITIVE: reference points for finding your way = shops, services, stops and monuments within autoData.places.landmarkRadiusM metres. 3 or more is fine, none is a total obstacle (a featureless street is hard to find your way in).

activities._comment: SOCIAL (activities): distance in metres to the nearest place to meet or take part in things (cafe, library, market, park, playground, place of worship...). 150 m or less is fine, 800 m or more is a total obstacle.

civic._comment: POLITICAL (memoire dimension 6, participation: accessible places for consultation, such as district town halls and project houses): distance in metres to the nearest place of local democracy and public service (town hall, community centre, social centre, courthouse, government office). 400 m or less is fine, 2000 m or more is a total obstacle. A proxy: OpenStreetMap cannot say who is actually heard.

noiseEstimate._comment: Used ONLY when no noise value is known. Estimate = base level of the nearest major road, plus/minus a speed correction, minus a drop with distance. The result is always marked 'estimated'. These are starting values: replace them with your own measurements when you have them. Needs major roads in the data; without them noise stays 'no data'.

autoData._comment: Values the program fills in BY ITSELF, so nothing has to be typed by hand. Each filled-in value is labelled with where it came from: 'official' (open government data), 'osm' (OpenStreetMap) or 'estimated' (a rule of thumb). A value you measure yourself always wins over all of these.

noiseMap._comment: Official road-noise map (Lden = 24-hour average) of Aix-Marseille-Provence Metropole, Licence Ouverte 2.0. Each band is stored by its lower limit (55, 60, 65, 70, 75). A segment gets the middle of its band: lower limit + bandMidpointOffsetDb. Anywhere outside every band is below 55 dB and gets belowThresholdDb. sampleSpacingM = how often along the segment the map is read (the average is used). This is a 24-hour average, not a midday reading. The map has gaps, including along parts of the Corniche: when a segment has NO band at all but a major road is within gapFallbackRoadM metres, the road-distance estimate (section noiseEstimate) is used instead and the value is labelled 'estimated'.

slope._comment: Slope worked out from official IGN altitude data (RGE ALTI) at the two ends of a segment. Segments shorter than minBaselineM stay 'no data': over a few metres the altitude error would give a wild slope.

widthDefaults._comment: STARTING GUESSES, not data: a typical width in metres per kind of path, used only when OSM has no width tag. They are labelled 'estimated' and never trigger a width veto. Replace them with what you actually measure, or delete a line to leave that kind of path at 'no data'.

excludeTrails._comment: Hiking trails are not pavements, so they are left out of the scoring. A walkway (path, footway or steps) is a trail when it carries any of the 'tags' (OSM hiking/mountain-bike tags), or its name starts with one of 'nameStartsWith', or it is a plain 'path' on one of the 'unpavedSurfaces'. Set the lists to [] to keep everything.

places._comment: Which OpenStreetMap places count for the cognitive and social indicators, and what 'near' means (metres).

zones._comment: How the program draws priority zones by itself, with no one marking anything. A segment is a candidate when its score for the chosen profile is below 'scoreBelow' (or it is vetoed). Candidates that touch, or lie within 'mergeGapM' metres of each other, join into one zone. A zone shorter than 'minLengthM' metres in total is dropped as noise, EXCEPT a zone containing a vetoed segment: a hard block is always kept. A single segment longer than 'maxSegmentM' metres (a rural road or an unbroken trail running for kilometres) is still scored and drawn but never listed as a zone: it cannot be pointed at as one place. A zone longer than 'maxLengthM' metres is split into pieces along a grid of 'splitCellM'-metre squares, so one chain of bad streets does not become a single zone of tens of kilometres. Zones are ranked by severity = sum over their segments of length x (1 - score).

classes._comment: Colour classes of the final score: below 'redBelow' = red, below 'orangeBelow' = orange, otherwise green. 'none' = not enough data to score.

profiles._howToAddProfile: To add a profile (elderly person, autistic person, stroller...), copy one block below, give it a new short name, and change: 'label', the 'weights' (they must add up to 1) and the 'vetoes'. A veto sets the score to 0 whenever it applies. Veto choices: stepsWithoutRamp (true/false), widthBelowM (a number of metres), kerbRaised (true/false). Leave 'vetoes' empty ({}) for none.
